newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures crash in late trade,tone weak.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures crash in late trade,tone weak.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures crashed through the floor in late Friday trade, with the benchmark March contract losing 975 points by the close in line with the Tokyo stock market's biggest one-day drop in two years.

The March contract settled at 17,175, precariously near its intra-day low of 17,080, against a previous close at 18,155. Turnover far exceeded the levels seen in recent months as a hefty 31,700 lots changed hands.
In Tokyo, the 225-share Nikkei average lost 770.22 points or 4.26 percent to end at 17,303.65.
"If we'd had another hour or so of trading, we could even have broken 17,000," said a trader with a U.S. house. "There was very little support below 17,800."
He said the March Nikkei looked set to break below 17,000 next week and it was likely to encounter some large stop-loss sell orders just under that level.
Dealers said there had been no fresh news to pull the market lower after four straight days of steep declines.
"The further it goes, the worse the outlook is," said the trader, adding that it was difficult to even pick a support level now.
"The main villains were the locals," said a trader with a European futures house.
He said stops were triggered at key technical levels and, "there was no looking back after that".
"Everyone is calling for 16,000 now. The institutional buyers are looking for that level to come back into the cash and futures," said a trader with a local house.

He said the market could try to find a base of support within a broader range of 16,100-17,100 in the near term, but it would need to climb above 17,550 fairly convincingly to dampen further selling interest. -- Sonali Desai (65-8703090)
